access_protocol.no_search: Do not hunt for credentials. Run the diagnostic you need: its access receipt names the effective source for each required authority. Use access_check.py to check the configured GitHub, GitLab and Kubernetes authorities.
access_protocol.rule: first match wins; the resolved source is reported in credential_sources
access_protocol.warning: The default kubeconfig may name another cluster. The selected context and API server are always verified before collection.

filters_records.--search: case-insensitive text filter over the returned records

namespaced.--namespace: one namespace, or `all`; `auto` where the command discovers it

access_check.py.purpose: Prove access to every selected authority and emit one receipt.
access_check.py.returns: A receipt: credential sources, identities, targets, skill digest, and one entry per live check.
access_check.py.use_when: When you need one live receipt for the configured GitHub, GitLab or Kubernetes authorities on the execution host.

bin/ci-api.execution_surface: installed Python command and one caller-selected provider API
bin/ci-api.purpose: Read one caller-selected GitHub or GitLab API endpoint with bounded output.
requires_authorities: one caller-selected GitHub or GitLab host
bin/ci-api.returns: Bounded JSON, YAML or selected text; dry-run returns a request plan.
bin/ci-api.use_when: A supported domain command does not expose the selected GET resource.

bin/ci-binary-build.execution_surface: installed Python command and local Git checkout; no cluster call
bin/ci-binary-build.purpose: Plan an exact-commit OpenShift Binary BuildConfig without applying it.
bin/ci-binary-build.returns: A JSON or YAML plan and fingerprint bound to one Git tree and BuildConfig.
bin/ci-binary-build.use_when: A selected BuildConfig and source commit need validation before a build.

ceph_cluster.py.purpose: Read Ceph health, root/rack/host/OSD hierarchy, inactive PGs, and OSD/monitor Pods.
ceph_cluster.py.returns: Ceph status, nested OSD tree, inactive PGs, and filtered OSD/monitor Pod records.
ceph_cluster.py.use_when: A selected Rook Ceph cluster needs API-backed diagnostics.

ceph_kernel.py.execution_surface: Kubernetes API and one existing Pod on the selected node
ceph_kernel.py.purpose: Classify host Ceph/RBD kernel journal lines through an existing Pod.
ceph_kernel.py.returns: Bounded UTC kernel records and read-only recommended action codes.
ceph_kernel.py.use_when: A selected node has a Pod with a verified host journal mount.

cilium_node.py.execution_surface: Kubernetes API and one existing Pod on the selected node
cilium_node.py.purpose: Read Cilium daemon status and health from an existing agent Pod on one node.
cilium_node.py.returns: One Pod record with bounded daemon and health summaries plus findings, or a classified failure.
cilium_node.py.use_when: A selected node needs Cilium daemon and peer diagnosis.

cilium_status.py.purpose: Aggregate Cilium agent, operator and node health by real exec.
cilium_status.py.returns: One record per agent with non-TTY health and actionable peer findings; UNKNOWN where exec could not run.
cilium_status.py.use_when: Connectivity is suspect, or a node's CNI may differ from its Ready condition.

create_selfhosted_runner.py.execution_surface: installed skill and configured provider APIs; GitHub Actions runs tests and lint only
create_selfhosted_runner.py.purpose: Build, publish, deploy and register a toolbox-backed GitHub runner.
create_selfhosted_runner.py.returns: Versioned operation plan or independently verified callback results, with cleanup evidence.
create_selfhosted_runner.py.side_effects: Only confirmed operations mutate selected resources; temporary helpers are cleaned on exit.
create_selfhosted_runner.py.use_when: Create, update or delete a GitHub runner using the configured cluster and Harbor.

event_trace.py.purpose: Return a time-ordered event trace from both event APIs.
event_trace.py.returns: One record per event, deduplicated across both APIs, oldest first.
event_trace.py.use_when: You need what the cluster said during an interval. Pass the interval; a zero count with zero errors means the events aged out, not that the read failed.

gitlab_access.py.purpose: Resolve the effective GitLab credential and read back identity and exact target.
gitlab_access.py.returns: The effective source, identity, origin, and numeric project or group ID.

check.purpose: read back GitLab identity and selected target

gitlab_access.py.use_when: Before a GitLab operation; this route needs GitLab access only.

gitlab_issue.py.purpose: Create or reuse an exact GitLab bug issue with independent read-back.
gitlab_issue.py.returns: A sanitized plan or verified issue IID and independent GET evidence.
gitlab_issue.py.side_effects: Confirmed apply may create the selected bug issue.
gitlab_issue.py.use_when: A selected project needs a requested bug issue.

gitlab_job.py.purpose: Get one CI job or list bounded jobs from one GitLab project.
gitlab_job.py.returns: Get: one job, pipeline, runner, and bounded trace. List: up to 500 validated job records, record_count and truncated; PARTIAL if the page scan cannot prove completeness.

get.purpose: read one exact job, pipeline, runner, and bounded trace

list.purpose: filter newest jobs of one verified project
list.read_back: GitLab project jobs keyset API; at most 20 pages of 100

gitlab_job.py.use_when: You need exact job facts or a filtered view of recent jobs.

gitlab_milestone.py.purpose: Create or update an exact GitLab milestone with independent read-back.
gitlab_milestone.py.returns: A sanitized plan or verified milestone record and independent GET evidence.
gitlab_milestone.py.side_effects: Confirmed apply may create or update the selected milestone.
gitlab_milestone.py.use_when: A selected project or group milestone needs a requested change.

gitlab_pipeline.py.purpose: Read, start, or watch an exact GitLab CI pipeline.
gitlab_pipeline.py.returns: Get returns one validated pipeline and bounded jobs. Start returns an offline or live plan, or a verified new or existing plan identity. Watch returns bounded graph completion, success, changes and retrieve choices.
gitlab_pipeline.py.side_effects: Confirmed start may create one pipeline on the selected ref.

get.purpose: Read one exact pipeline and its bounded jobs.
get.read_back: GitLab pipeline and job APIs for the selected numeric ID.

start.purpose: Resolve an exact ref and commit, then start one confirmed pipeline.
start.read_back: GET the exact pipeline and variables; require project, ref, SHA and plan marker.
start.side_effects: Confirmed apply creates one pipeline or returns NO_OP for its verified plan marker.

watch.purpose: Watch one bounded pipeline graph to settlement or timeout.
watch.read_back: Poll root, child, related and job state through bounded GitLab reads.

gitlab_pipeline.py.use_when: You need exact pipeline state, a confirmed start, or bounded completion evidence.

gitlab_runner.py.purpose: Read and manage a selected GitLab runner record with verified actions.
gitlab_runner.py.returns: Public runner fields, a sanitized plan, or verified before/after action evidence.
gitlab_runner.py.side_effects: Apply may create, assign, tag, or delete a runner record.

assign.purpose: Assign an existing runner to the selected project or group.
assign.read_back: Read scoped runner membership after assignment.
assign.side_effects: Apply may attach a runner to selected projects.

create.purpose: Create a runner record and save its one-time token.
create.read_back: Read the new runner record and scoped listing.
create.side_effects: Apply may create a runner record and write the token file.

delete.purpose: Delete one runner by ID after a live plan binds its identity and project assignments.
delete.read_back: Require global 404 and absence from the selected scope.
delete.side_effects: Apply deletes the selected runner record.

get.purpose: Read one runner by ID, exact unique description, or related project job ID.
get.read_back: Read the selected job when given, then runner details and selected-scope membership.

list.purpose: List bounded scoped runners with optional exact description and state filters.
list.read_back: Read each matching runner from the bound GitLab API.

tag.purpose: Add tags to an existing runner record.
tag.read_back: Read tags from a fresh runner GET and scoped listing.
tag.side_effects: Apply may update the runner tag list.

gitlab_runner.py.use_when: A job names a runner to inspect, or a project needs runner record management.

gitlab_runner_manager.py.execution_surface: installed skill, configured provider APIs, and the caller-selected digest-pinned toolbox image
gitlab_runner_manager.py.purpose: Deploy or remove one toolbox-backed GitLab shell runner.
gitlab_runner_manager.py.returns: A run ID and confirmed plan, or verified workload and exact GitLab runner read-back with cleanup evidence.
gitlab_runner_manager.py.side_effects: Deploy uses GitLab, Kubernetes and Harbor; delete uses GitLab and Kubernetes only. Provider runner deletion remains gitlab_runner.py delete.

delete.read_back: Owned Deployment and Secrets absent, exact runner record preserved with its current cached status, run-owned SCC RoleBinding absent, and owned generated namespace absent.
delete.side_effects: Confirmed apply removes only run-owned manager resources and preserves the GitLab runner record.

deploy.read_back: Exact-node privileged Deployment and immutable Pod image, then the exact scoped GitLab runner online with contact evidence.
deploy.side_effects: Confirmed apply opens or reuses one run scope, creates a run-owned SCC RoleBinding only when required, and retains the verified manager workload.

gitlab_runner_manager.py.use_when: A pre-created project or group runner must execute on the exact worker proven ready for Podman.

gitlab_wiki.py.purpose: Create or update an exact GitLab wiki page with independent read-back.
gitlab_wiki.py.returns: A sanitized plan or verified wiki slug and independent GET evidence.
gitlab_wiki.py.side_effects: Confirmed apply may create or update the selected wiki page.
gitlab_wiki.py.use_when: A selected project wiki page needs requested content.

harbor_pull.py.execution_surface: installed skill and configured provider APIs; GitHub Actions runs tests and lint only
harbor_pull.py.purpose: Pull a Harbor toolbox in Kubernetes and execute its doctor.
harbor_pull.py.returns: Versioned operation plan or independently verified callback results, with cleanup evidence.
harbor_pull.py.side_effects: Only confirmed operations mutate selected resources; temporary helpers are cleaned on exit.
harbor_pull.py.use_when: Prove a published toolbox image works, with temporary Job cleanup.

harbor_push.py.execution_surface: installed skill and configured provider APIs; GitHub Actions runs tests and lint only
harbor_push.py.purpose: Copy a selected image to Harbor and verify the immutable digest.
harbor_push.py.returns: Versioned operation plan or independently verified callback results, with cleanup evidence.
harbor_push.py.side_effects: Only confirmed operations mutate selected resources; temporary helpers are cleaned on exit.
harbor_push.py.use_when: Publish an existing image without building or creating a runner.

image_build_readiness.py.execution_surface: configured Kubernetes API and a temporary privileged Job
image_build_readiness.py.purpose: Probe nested Podman execution on one Kubernetes worker and clean up.
image_build_readiness.py.returns: A plan or nested-runtime evidence with the Pod exit code, marker rows and cleanup read-back; does not prove runner or image-publication behavior.
image_build_readiness.py.side_effects: Apply creates a run-owned namespace, conditionally creates one namespaced SCC RoleBinding, then creates a script ConfigMap and Job; it removes only resources owned by the run.

probe.purpose: Run a temporary Podman Job on one selected worker.
probe.read_back: Exact permission source, optional RoleBinding UID, Job-owned Pod exit, probe rows and resource absence.
probe.side_effects: Creates and removes a temporary namespace, conditional run-owned SCC RoleBinding, script ConfigMap and privileged Job.

image_build_readiness.py.use_when: Check container execution, bind mounts and exit propagation before building a runner workflow.

k8s_verify_mtu_consistency.py.execution_surface: OpenShift API and temporary oc debug Pods
k8s_verify_mtu_consistency.py.purpose: Compare PCI Ethernet uplink MTUs across selected Kubernetes nodes.
k8s_verify_mtu_consistency.py.returns: A versioned table of node, PCI NIC, optional IPv4 address and MTU, consistency findings, and temporary-Pod cleanup read-back.
k8s_verify_mtu_consistency.py.side_effects: oc debug creates temporary Pods; apply verifies their cleanup
k8s_verify_mtu_consistency.py.use_when: An OpenShift Ceph or Cilium symptom may involve physical NIC MTUs; plan the selected nodes, then run the exact confirmed plan.

ocp_node_onboard.py.execution_surface: installed skill controls tools, ISO generation and node join in the selected cluster
ocp_node_onboard.py.purpose: Build an OpenShift node ISO in-cluster, join its node, and verify selected storage.
ocp_node_onboard.py.returns: Shared workflow report with native completion, join read-back, final cluster artifact identity/lifetime, plan, provenance and cleanup evidence.
ocp_node_onboard.py.side_effects: Build/join/remove use plan confirmation. Native oc creates temporary build resources; join approves only the selected node's two signers. ISO bytes stay in the cluster.

build.purpose: Build from either a MAC or native YAML and verify the exact cluster destination.
build.read_back: Native completion, embedded Ignition, actual ISO size/SHA-256 and destination.
build.side_effects: Confirmed build stages a tool Pod and native OpenShift temporary resources, writes the requested ISO, and retains its run record; temporary final storage retains its Pod.

join.purpose: Approve the booted node's selected CSRs and verify its Ready identity.
join.read_back: Client bootstrap-completion evidence, issued serving request state and exact Ready Node hostname, roles and observed IPs.
join.side_effects: Confirmed join approves only the exact hostname's client and serving signers, then removes the owned build scope; it never boots or deletes a node.

remove.purpose: Remove owned run resources while preserving persistent destination storage and ISO.
remove.read_back: Owned resource absence and, for persistent output, unchanged ISO before and after removal.
remove.side_effects: Confirmed removal deletes only run-owned resources; temporary output ends with its Pod. Persistent ISO and caller storage remain.

verify.purpose: Read and inspect the existing cluster-held ISO identified by its run.
verify.read_back: Exact stored artifact identity, size/SHA-256 and embedded Ignition.
verify.side_effects: Persistent storage can require a temporary reader Pod, cleaned after inspection.

ocp_node_onboard.py.use_when: Prepare a node boot image from the caller's native MAC or YAML input; join its booted node, inspect it or release a previous run. See references/ocp-node-image.md.

prepare_tool_pod.py.execution_surface: installed skill controls a Pod in the selected Kubernetes cluster
prepare_tool_pod.py.purpose: Prepare, reuse or remove a cluster Pod with declared tools.
prepare_tool_pod.py.returns: Plan or actual Pod identity, tool observations, per-callback results and cleanup.
prepare_tool_pod.py.side_effects: Confirmed prepare creates and retains run-owned resources; remove deletes only those resources. Failure removes resources created by the failed run.
prepare_tool_pod.py.use_when: Run tooling in a retained cluster Pod for another callback or command.

reference.py.description: One answer per node: installed tools to run and references to read, each a pointer to the next call.
reference.py.execution_surface: installed catalogue; no provider or credential access

output_modes.human: Run and read lists; default on a terminal
output_modes.json: Compact JSON; default when stdout is not a terminal

reference.py.purpose: Show what the agent can run and read at one node, or read one reference.
reference.py.returns: A node of tools and references, one reference's sections, or one section's own text.
reference.py.side_effects: Only an explicit log file is written; dry-run and describe do not write.
reference.py.use_when: Choose a cluster or command, list a reference's sections or read one section.

storage_report.py.purpose: Correlate claims, volumes, attachments, pods and controllers.
storage_report.py.returns: One record per claim or standalone volume, with its pods, attachments and controllers.
storage_report.py.use_when: A workload will not start or a volume looks stuck, and you need the chain.

toolbox.py.execution_surface: installed skill and configured provider APIs; GitHub Actions runs tests and lint only
toolbox.py.purpose: Build or delete a toolbox using the configured OpenShift and Harbor.
toolbox.py.returns: Versioned operation plan or independently verified callback results, with cleanup evidence.
toolbox.py.side_effects: Only confirmed operations mutate selected resources; temporary helpers are cleaned on exit.
toolbox.py.use_when: Build one validated toolbox specification independently of a runner.

default_output: json when stdout is not a terminal, human when it is

exit_codes.0: PASS, DRY_RUN, or a live read-only PLANNED result
exit_codes.2: BLOCKED or PARTIAL, or an input that could not be used

node_local_options.--binding: project binding for target and ordered kubeconfig sources
node_local_options.--describe: this command's machine-readable contract, then exit
node_local_options.--dry-run: list API and existing-Pod probes without executing them
node_local_options.--human: human summary even when stdout is not a terminal
node_local_options.--revision: exact source commit of the installed copy, recorded as a claim
node_local_options.--search: case-insensitive text filter over returned records

status_values.BLOCKED: an authority or a required read failed; see blocking_live_checks
status_values.DRY_RUN: a probe plan only, never access evidence
status_values.PARTIAL: the read completed and a component is unhealthy; see access_proven
status_values.PASS: every selected authority and live check passed
status_values.PLANNED: a live read-only operation plan, with no resource mutation
status_values.UNKNOWN: a per-item reading could not be taken, preserved rather than coerced

target_protocol.when: set; a missing file is an error, never a fallback
present in the working directory; ci-skills-smoke selects ci-skills-smoke.toml instead
present; ci-skills-smoke selects ci-skills-smoke.toml instead, without normal-target fallback

universal_options.--binding: project-declared target and ordered kubeconfig source resolver
universal_options.--describe: this command's machine-readable contract, then exit
universal_options.--dry-run: list planned probes without contacting any API; never access evidence
universal_options.--human: human summary even when stdout is not a terminal
universal_options.--log-file: also append sanitized diagnostics to this exact path
universal_options.--log-format: diagnostic log format: text or JSON Lines (default: text)
universal_options.--log-level: minimum diagnostic level: debug, info, warning, or error
universal_options.--output-dir: write paired JSON and text reports to this explicit path
universal_options.--revision: exact source commit of the installed copy, recorded as a claim
universal_options.--run-id: caller-selected identifier included in diagnostic logs
